newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cargill Brazil to invest $5 mln more in wheat mill.
newsitem.headline: Cargill Brazil to invest $5 mln more in wheat mill.

text.p: The Brazilian arm of U.S. grains giant Cargill Inc plans to invest $5 million over the next six months in expanding capacity at its wheat mill in Sao Paulo state, the marketing head of the grains division said.
"We are planning the expansion of our mill in Tatui, which should be completed in six to seven months," Sergio Andrade told Reuters.
The enlargement is part of Cargill's planned overall investments of $300 million in the region until the year 2000.
"Within that sum, I would say a significant part -- although I can't say exactly what number -- is destined to the wheat sector," Andrade said.

The Sao Valentin mill in Tatui currently has a milling capacity of 500 tonnes per day and this should increase to 800 to 900 tonnes after the expansion, he said. "We're talking about a capacity expansion of the order of 70 percent," he said.
Cargill bought the mill last September for $20 million and is studying the purchase of several other wheat mills in Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais states, Andrade added.
"The timeframe depends very much on opportunity, a lot on negotiations, but by the year 2000 we should have at least two more wheat mills," he said.

The Sao Valentin mill is expected to bring in $50 million over the next 12 months, calculated at its current capacity. It earned $4 million in May, Andrade said.
Cargill has recently completed the transfer of the mill's former brandnames to its own Letizia brand, which is also available in Argentina, and is looking at producing a range of new products.
Among these is a ready-made mix for French bread which Andrade describes as "a first step in the strategy of adding value to flour".

Cargill is also claiming a stake in the rapidly expanding domestic market for durum semolina, used in the fabrication of pasta, as the Sao Valentin mill is the only one in Brazil with a milling capacity for hard wheat, Andrade said.
